{"path":"SOLUTION.md","content":"# Solution

Two bugs in `lrucache/cache.py`:

1. **`get` did not refresh recency.** A successful `get` returned the value but
   never moved the key to the most-recently-used end of the `OrderedDict`, so a
   recently-read entry could still be evicted. Fixed by calling
   `self._data.move_to_end(key)` on a non-expired hit.

2. **`put` evicted an entry even when updating an existing key.** The
   capacity check ran unconditionally before insertion, so overwriting a key in
   a full cache evicted the LRU entry even though no new slot was needed. Fixed
   by only evicting when the key is not already present
   (`if key not in self._data and len(self._data) >= self.capacity`).
"}

content:
Done. The full suite passes (6/6) and `SOLUTION.md` is written.

The two bugs, both in `lrucache/cache.py`:

- `get()` never refreshed recency — a hit didn't move the key to the MRU end, so a freshly-read entry could still be evicted (`cache.py:30` now calls `move_to_end`).
- `put()` evicted unconditionally at capacity, even when just updating an existing key — now it only evicts when inserting a *new* key into a full cache (`cache.py:34`).

No changes under `tests/`; nothing committed to git.
